speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Gilbert? Will. From Great St Helen's, with a face like a pudding. God give you joy of the day.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: Brother. Gilbert. From my lodging in St Bride's. Twenty-nine, if the almanac is honest.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then joy of it. I can say the word. I cannot chew a feast.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: The money went down safe by the carrier of the second. A Stratford wool-man at the Bell on Saturday brought the word back, and a cheese with it. Mother's make. A whole one. The note says half is yours.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Half is a kindness I cannot use.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: You can't chew. I'll eat your half and call it my birthday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Eat it. I am not sending anyone for a cheese I can only look at. Keep it where it is.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: The frame they raised in August is thatched, and it stands. Father says it's the first thing a player ever held up.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Tell him I heard the sentence. I will not improve it.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: I will not improve it either. It arrived whole. How is the pudding?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The tooth comes out tomorrow at ten.

speaker: gilbert_shakespeare
text: I'd have done it for six with the shop pliers. God keep you, brother.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And you. Keep me the rind.
